reading.body:
Wyoming's data-center footprint, as recorded here, consists of four facilities, three of them clustered within roughly one kilometer of each other in the Cheyenne and Laramie County area near the Colorado border.

Two of the four are Microsoft-operated campuses, CYS41 and CYS42, sitting adjacent to the NCAR-Wyoming Supercomputing Center run by the University Corporation for Atmospheric Research. That proximity is not explained by the data, but the concentration of compute infrastructure in a single tight geography means that local power and land availability are the shared constraints for all three. The fourth facility, Windbreak Cable in Pine Bluffs, stands apart with no operator listed.

The dataset records zero total megawatts across all four facilities. That figure most likely reflects missing data rather than zero power draw, and readers should treat capacity as unknown rather than negligible. What the data does establish is the shape of Wyoming's footprint: small in count, geographically narrow, and anchored by a pair of large-operator campuses whose power demands are not yet visible here.
